screening.reason: Inclusion 2/3: analyses ABIDE I resting-state fMRI (C-PAC-preprocessed BOLD time series) explicitly, combined with an anatomical-distance graph topology, and reports a diagnostic prediction (ASD vs. neurotypical classification) analysis.

evidence_spans.text:
In this study, we consider the ABIDE I preprocessed dataset (Di Martino
et al., 2014; Craddock et al., 2013). It includes BOLD time-series extracted
from rs-fMRI through a preprocessing pipeline which is fully detailed on the web
platforms related to the ABIDE collection
evidence_spans.claim: Uses the ABIDE I Preprocessed Connectomes Project dataset of rs-fMRI BOLD time series.

evidence_spans.text:
The time-series consid-
ered in our work were preprocessed according to the C-PAC pipeline, which
involves the following main steps: basic processing, noise signal removal, global
regression, band-pass ﬁltering (0.01-0.1 Hz), registration, time-series extrac-
tion
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing pipeline: C-PAC (basic processing, nuisance/global signal regression, band-pass filtering 0.01-0.1 Hz, registration).

evidence_spans.text:
The selected mean time-series
correspond to the Automated Anatomical Labeling atlas on 90 regions of interest
(AAL90)
evidence_spans.claim: AAL90 atlas used for ROI time-series extraction.
Explicit inclusion criteria: eyes-open scans, age under 18, mean framewise displacement under 0.2 mm.

evidence_spans.text:
The corresponding data subset consists of a total of 452 subjects, with respec-
tively 251 NT and 201 ASD subjects.
evidence_spans.claim: Primary analysed cohort: 452 ABIDE I adolescent subjects (201 ASD, 251 neurotypical).

evidence_spans.claim: The proposed combined structural+functional graph-signal-processing framework outperforms GFT and single-modality state-of-the-art classification methods.

evidence_spans.text:
The analysis of the results reveals the inﬂuence of the frontal and temporal

This

evidence_spans.claim: Predictive markers implicate frontal and temporal lobe regions in ASD classification, consistent with prior neuroscience literature.

assessments.support: 452 ABIDE I adolescents (201 ASD, 251 NT) selected via explicit inclusion criteria (eyes-open, age<18, mean FD<0.2mm); a separate 130-subject adult subsample (63 ASD, 67 NT) used for generalization assessment.
C-PAC pipeline and AAL90 atlas named explicitly; anatomical k-nearest-neighbor graph topology for the 'structural' component fully described.
ASD/NT labels drawn from the ABIDE phenotypic file; the paper does not restate the diagnostic instrument/criteria used to assign group membership.

Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation is used given the small sample, with inner cross-validation for hyperparameter tuning on each training split (reducing leakage risk), but no site-aware (leave-site-out) evaluation is reported despite the dataset spanning 17 ABIDE sites.

risk_of_bias.summary: A well-documented predictive ABIDE I study combining structural (anatomical-distance graph) and functional (rs-fMRI) information, with explicit motion/age/eyes-open inclusion criteria and inner cross-validated hyperparameter tuning, though site heterogeneity (17 sites) is not addressed via leave-site-out evaluation.

charting.title: Combining Anatomical and Functional Networks for Neuropathology Identification: A Case Study on Autism Spectrum Disorder
charting.age_range: under 18 years (primary sample); 18-50 years (adult generalization subsample)
charting.data_types: resting-state fMRI; anatomical (geometric distance) graph topology
charting.feature_types: graph signal processing features (frequency content of rs-fMRI signals on a brain graph)
charting.specific_features: Graph Fourier Transform (GFT) coefficients of rs-fMRI BOLD signals over an anatomical k-nearest-neighbor brain graph (AAL90 ROIs), projected via an extended Fukunaga-Koontz transform
charting.importance_method: Decision-tree interpretable splits on graph-frequency features
charting.specific_algorithms: Graph Signal Processing (Fukunaga-Koontz transform extension) feature extraction + decision tree classifier, compared against GFT and Structural Feature Method (SFM) baselines
charting.validation_methodology: Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation with inner cross-validation for hyperparameter tuning on each training split
charting.key_performance_results: Averaged test accuracy of 73.5% (m=2), 74.8% (m=3), 73.0% (m=4) and 71.3% (m=5), significantly outperforming the SFM baseline (e.g. 69.1%-70.4%) at 95% training set size (p<=0.026); on an adult generalization subsample the proposed framework outperformed SFM by up to a 15-percentage-point gap
charting.summary_key_findings: A graph-signal-processing framework combining an anatomical (geometric nearest-neighbor) brain graph with rs-fMRI BOLD signal frequency content, classified via an interpretable decision tree, outperforms structural-only (SFM) and functional-only (GFT) state-of-the-art baselines on a 452-subject ABIDE I adolescent cohort (201 ASD, 251 NT), with predictive markers implicating frontal and temporal lobe regions.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Frontal and temporal lobe graph-frequency features
charting.reviewer_notes: A secondary 130-subject adult ABIDE I subsample (63 ASD, 67 NT, ages 18-50) was used only to assess generalization of the framework, not as the primary analysed cohort.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction; ABIDE I; 452 adolescents (201 ASD, 251 neurotypical) from 17 sites (primary sample), plus a 130-subject adult generalization subsample (63 ASD, 67 NT)
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI BOLD signals over AAL90 ROIs combined with an anatomical k-nearest-neighbor brain graph; Graph Signal Processing (extended Fukunaga-Koontz transform) features classified via an interpretable decision tree; Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation with inner CV for hyperparameter tuning
narrative_row.outcomes: Averaged test accuracy up to 74.8% (m=3), significantly outperforming a structural-only (SFM) baseline and a functional-only (GFT) baseline; predictive markers implicate frontal and temporal lobe regions; framework also generalizes to an independent adult subsample with up to a 15-point accuracy gap over SFM
narrative_row.key_limitations: No leave-site-out evaluation despite 17-site heterogeneity; diagnostic-instrument source not restated; 'structural' network is an anatomical-distance graph rather than a diffusion-derived structural connectome
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates that combining a geometric/anatomical brain graph with rs-fMRI graph-signal features improves interpretable ASD classification over single-modality baselines on a well-specified ABIDE I adolescent subset

kg_link.cohort_description: 452 ABIDE I adolescent participants (201 ASD, 251 neurotypical) from 17 sites, selected for eyes-open acquisition, age under 18, and mean framewise displacement under 0.2mm; a secondary 130-subject adult subsample (63 ASD, 67 NT) used for generalization
kg_link.finding: A graph-signal-processing framework combining an anatomical brain graph with rs-fMRI BOLD signal frequency content achieves up to 74.8% averaged test accuracy classifying ASD vs. neurotypical participants, outperforming structural-only and functional-only baselines, with frontal and temporal lobe regions identified as most predictive.
